defects.description: Step 5 adds a local writePrefsError that writes a flat {code, field} body, bypassing httpx.Error and the {"error": {code, message, details}} envelope that every existing endpoint returns (devices.RegisterHandler uses httpx.Error with details.field for 422s).

Error codes and field paths drift from R3/AC4: bad_timezone instead of invalid_timezone, and Go struct names (QuietHours.TZ, Categories.Social) instead of JSON paths (quiet_hours.timezone, categories.social). AC4 fails.

InQuietHours uses startMin <= nowMin < endMin, which never matches a window that crosses midnight (22:00-07:00), so AC3 fails. The planned quiet_test only uses a same-day 09:00-17:00 window and no sender test covers AC3's 22:00-07:00 Berlin cases (23:30 suppressed, 07:00 delivered).
defects.location: plan.md step 6; plan.md Test strategy; spec.md R4, AC3

defects.description: Timezone validation and quiet-hours conversion use time.LoadLocation, but both binaries are built CGO_ENABLED=0 into distroless/static, which ships no zoneinfo. Every timezone would fail validation and quiet hours could not be evaluated unless time/tzdata is embedded (import _ "time/tzdata" or -tags timetzdata).

Step 7 fails open: when the preferences lookup fails, Send continues with Defaults() (all categories enabled), so a user who turned marketing off receives marketing pushes during any database error. This contradicts the spec's non-functional constraint that a marketing push must never reach a user whose saved preferences turn marketing off.
defects.location: plan.md step 7; spec.md Non-functional constraints (marketing consent)

defects.description: The new Prefs.Get lookup in Send has no deadline. The worker's job loop calls Send with context.Background() and Sender.Timeout only wraps the per-device Push, so a slow or stalled notification_preferences query blocks the sequential batch (while it holds the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED transaction) and breaks the 5 ms p99 sender budget. The lookup needs its own short timeout.
Step 8 hand-rolls a CachedReader (map + RWMutex) instead of reusing internal/cache.TTL, the bounded TTL cache the worker already uses through devices.NewCachedRepo in cmd/worker/main.go.

The CachedReader never expires entries and is unbounded. The API and the worker are separate processes (cmd/api, cmd/worker; three worker replicas in deploy/worker.yaml) and each builds its own CachedReader, so PutHandler's Invalidate only clears the API's copy. The worker keeps serving the first document it read until restart, violating the 60-second constraint and AC3 in production, and memory grows with every user pushed.
defects.location: plan.md steps 8-9; fixture/cmd/worker/main.go; fixture/deploy/worker.yaml; spec.md Non-functional constraints

tensions.description: Risk wants the unbounded preferences lookup given a short timeout; consistency wants the fail-open fallback replaced by fail-closed (return the error, send nothing) to honour marketing consent. Together, every lookup timeout or error now makes Send return an error. Two facts sit elsewhere: the worker's runBatch (cmd/worker/main.go) deletes each job after one attempt whatever Send returns, and step 7 runs the lookup before the security bypass. So the combined fixes permanently drop every push during a slow query, including security pushes that R4 says are always delivered. Neither fix shows the problem alone: with fail-open a timeout is harmless, and without a timeout fail-closed only fires on hard errors.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Wrap Prefs.Get in a short context.WithTimeout so a slow preferences query cannot stall the worker or blow the 5 ms budget.
tensions.lens_b_fix: On a lookup error, return the error from Send and deliver nothing, so a marketing opt-out is never overridden by Defaults().
tensions.reconciliation: Keep the timeout, but move the security bypass ahead of the lookup so security pushes never depend on the preferences table. On lookup error or timeout, fail closed only for marketing (the one category the spec ties to consent) and deliver social and reminders under Defaults(). Do not rely on returning the error, because runBatch deletes the job after a single attempt. This needs risk's fact (at-most-once job deletion in cmd/worker/main.go, plus the lookup-before-security ordering) and consistency's fact (the consent constraint covers marketing only).

tensions.description: Architecture wants the hand-rolled CachedReader replaced by internal/cache.TTL, wired the way cmd/worker/main.go wires devices.NewCachedRepo with the shared CACHE_TTL/CACHE_SIZE. That looks right: the code default for CACHE_TTL is 1 minute. Risk wants the never-expiring cache given its own short expiry (for example 30 s) and a size bound, since cross-process Invalidate cannot reach the worker. The fixes conflict on the TTL. deploy/worker.yaml sets CACHE_TTL=10m, so the reuse as wired would serve preferences up to 10 minutes stale and break the 60-second constraint. Risk's version keeps a second bespoke cache.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Delete prefs/cache.go and wrap the prefs repo with cache.New(cacheSize, cacheTTL) in cmd/worker/main.go, as the devices repo is.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Add a 30-second expiry and a maximum size to CachedReader and stop relying on PutHandler's Invalidate for the worker.
tensions.reconciliation: Reuse internal/cache.TTL, but give preferences their own TTL of 60 s or less (for example a PREFS_CACHE_TTL defaulting to 30s) and their own size, not the shared CACHE_TTL that deploy/worker.yaml overrides to 10m. Drop cross-process Invalidate as a correctness mechanism; the API can read through without caching. This needs architecture's fact (internal/cache.TTL and the worker's wiring) and risk's fact (separate API and worker processes, plus the 10m production value in deploy/worker.yaml against the spec's 60 s).

tensions.description: Architecture wants writePrefsError replaced with httpx.Error so the body uses the API-wide {"error": {...}} envelope. Consistency wants the body to match R3/AC4 literally: flat {code, field} with invalid_timezone and quiet_hours.timezone. Switching to httpx.Error changes the shape AC4 asserts, while fixing the drift literally keeps a one-off body shape no other endpoint uses.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Use httpx.Error(w, 422, code, message, details) like devices.RegisterHandler.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Emit exactly {"code": "invalid_timezone", "field": "quiet_hours.timezone"} with the spec's codes and JSON paths.
tensions.reconciliation: Use httpx.Error with status 422, the spec's code names (invalid_preferences, invalid_time, invalid_timezone) and details.field set to the JSON path, following the details.field convention in devices/handler.go. Flag to the spec owner that R3/AC4's flat shape differs from the envelope every endpoint returns, and get AC4 amended to assert error.code and error.details.field.
